leading_positions.synthesis: Four of six members explicitly prefer B046 as a single-part prize crediting Daniel J. Drucker, Jens Juul Holst and Lotte Bjerre Knudsen, with a citation covering both the physiology of GLP-1 and its development into incretin therapies. They share the view that the translational arc is part of the achievement and that a developer should be credited alongside the physiologists. Each of the four also states that the omission of Svetlana Mojsov, and of the Habener group, is a real weakness, and none claims to have verified the priority record. El-Manira and Linnarsson say they would accept or revisit a Mojsov-for-Knudsen swap if the record or a discovery-only framing warranted it; Sandberg and Svenningsson would want the committee to examine the record first.

Two of six members explicitly prefer B046 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, a discovery-centred trio whose citation covers the physiology and the identification of the active GLP-1 form. They share with the first group the same prize part, the same scientific assessment and the same two core names, and differ only in the third laureate and in citation emphasis. Perlmann states that he would move toward the Knudsen trio if Mojsov's work cannot be separated from the Habener group or verified. Wahren-Herlenius is the more settled on Mojsov and treats Knudsen as the point on which she is least settled, but both note that their agreement rests on recollection rather than verification.

areas_of_agreement: All six members place B046 (GLP-1 and incretin therapies) in their preferred configuration as a single-part prize, and all six describe it as mature, independently confirmed and supported by large randomized outcome data in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal endpoints.
All six name Daniel J. Drucker and Jens Juul Holst as laureates for B046.
Every member's alternatives are drawn from B037 (CAR-T) and B014 (unfolded protein response); no member lists another shortlisted candidate as an alternative in the round-1 configuration.

Members agree that B030 (optogenetics) is scientifically exceptional as a method but that six credited names against a three-person cap make a defensible trio difficult, and that it should not compete with B046 this year.

Members agree that B014 has the cleanest attribution (Walter and Mori) on the shortlist, with the caveat that the PERK and ATF6 arms (Ron and others) lie outside the pair and clinical translation is still emerging.
scientific_disputes: Whether the B046 citation should be physiology-led (discovery of GLP-1 biology and the active peptide) or should equally credit the drug-development arc to long-acting analogues; members differ in how much weight they give discovery versus translation, not in their assessment of the science.

Whether B014 should be treated as a rival for first place, a strong fallback, or a possible second part, given that its mechanism is complete and original but its human-disease consequences are described by several members as largely prospective.

Whether optogenetics (B030), as an enabling method rather than a disease-altering discovery, fits a Physiology or Medicine prize; members cite this together with its credit problem, and the committee has not separated the two arguments.

Whether TNF blockade (B021), raised by Wahren-Herlenius as mature and arguably overdue, has enough conceptual originality to be a fallback; El-Manira and Svenningsson rank it below CAR-T and the unfolded protein response, and Perlmann notes it is a single-member candidate.
attribution_disputes: B046 laureate set: four members credit Drucker, Holst and Knudsen; two credit Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The two trios differ only in the third name. Mojsov's priority for identifying and synthesising the active GLP-1 peptide relative to the Habener group is described as contested or unverified by every member who addresses it, and the Habener group is not among the supplied names.

Whether a cap of three can credit both the academic discoverers and the industrial developer of liraglutide and semaglutide without dropping either Mojsov or Knudsen; no member proposes a way to include all four credited names.

B037 (CAR-T): Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept lies outside the credited names (June, Sadelain, Rosenberg) according to El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius, and is the stated reason that members keep it as an alternative rather than above B046.
B030 (optogenetics): six credited names, with live disputes over Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenboeck and the first neuronal demonstration, so any trio excludes a contributor with a serious claim.
maturity_disputes: No member disputes the maturity of B046; members describe GLP-1 science as confirmed independently for decades, though El-Manira and Svenningsson note that long-term safety and durability of chronic incretin therapy for obesity are still accumulating.

B014 is described as mature mechanistically but immature in clinical consequence; Sandberg treats a single-part B014 prize as plausible if B046 stalls on credit, whereas El-Manira and Wahren-Herlenius weight demonstrated patient benefit more heavily and place it behind CAR-T.

B030 is described by several members as early in clinical benefit, while B021 is described as fully mature, so the shortlist mixes candidates whose maturity problem is too little translation with candidates whose problem is limited conceptual originality.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson (chair) discloses about twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy) and a Rockefeller postdoc with Paul Greengard; neither involves a shortlisted candidate, noted for transparency only.
El-Manira discloses a 2009 co-authored paper with Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons, and notes that his motor-circuit field is adjacent to optogenetics (B030), which he does not propose.

Linnarsson discloses co-authorship of the 2016 spatial-transcriptomics paper and prior co-authorships with Sandberg, none involving a shortlisted candidate, and notes his single-cell genomics field is unrelated to the shortlisted achievements.

Perlmann discloses collaborations with Ronald Evans and Johan Ericson (nuclear receptors, dopamine neurons) and co-authorship with Svenningsson and El-Manira on other topics; none is a shortlisted candidate.
Sandberg discloses co-authorship with Linnarsson and Frisen, and notes that his RNA processing and single-cell field is closest to B043, which is not in his preferred configuration.

Wahren-Herlenius notes that her autoimmunity and rheumatology field is close to the TNF-blockade candidate B021, which is not in her preferred configuration; her documented co-authors and Bergen affiliation do not connect to any proposed laureate.
No member reports a conflict that requires recusal on B046, B037 or B014.
questions_for_round2: What does the documented record show about Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide relative to the Habener group: is her contribution independent and necessary to the discovery, or joint and inseparable? Which members will change their third laureate for B046 depending on the answer?

Should the B046 citation be framed as a discovery prize (physiology and the active peptide) or as a discovery-to-therapy prize? If the latter, can the committee defend leaving out Mojsov, and if the former, can it defend leaving out Knudsen?
Is there any defensible way to treat the omitted Habener group and the fourth credited name as outside the prize, and what wording of the citation would make that exclusion explicit and principled?

If B046 stalls on credit, which fallback does each member support as a stand-alone prize, B037 or B014, and what attribution would each require given Eshhar's omitted chimeric receptor concept and the omitted PERK and ATF6 arms?

Should a second prize part be added to B046 at all? Linnarsson and Svenningsson see no clear gain, and Sandberg notes that pairing B014 would make four laureates against the cap of three in total; do any members want a multi-part configuration, and with which names?
Does any member want to move B030, B021 or B044 into the final configuration, and if so what trio or pair would they name and how would they resolve the stated credit and originality objections?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows complete agreement that B046 is the prize and that Drucker and Holst are two of its laureates, with disagreement confined to the third name (Knudsen for four members, Mojsov for two) and to whether the citation emphasises discovery or translation. Every member who addresses it says the Mojsov priority record is unverified and that the Habener group falls outside the supplied names, so the supplied evidence cannot yet settle the split. Fallback preferences are concentrated on B037 and B014, with no member proposing a different second candidate in their preferred configuration.
